observation.visible_scene: A tight close-up of an aircraft propeller: a dark, glossy spinner cone (marked with small specks and a diagonal light streak) with several long blades tipped in yellow/gold, set against a heavily blurred cityscape of tall buildings, as seen from a moving aircraft.
visible_changes: The orientation of the blade cluster relative to the frame drifts gradually over the excerpt: the left and right blades rise toward horizontal-up and the upper blade leans further to the right, so the whole propeller assembly appears to turn slowly.

The framing tightens on the hub toward the end: the spinner cone occupies more of the image, the blades look thinner/more edge-on (foreshortened), and the dark lower air-intake opening with its yellow rim becomes progressively more visible.
The blurred background shifts and brightens (building masses slide and the right side washes out to near-white), indicating camera movement/zoom alongside the apparent blade rotation.
Blades remain sharply defined with no motion-blur disc in any frame, so any spin is slow relative to the sampling rate.
uncertain_details: Whether the change in blade angle is true propeller rotation or camera roll/rotation is not separable from the blurred background; the lack of blur could mean a slow spin or a near-stationary prop.
The direction of the apparent rotation and the exact blade count (looks like 4–5) are not firmly established.
Whether the aircraft itself is translating is inferred only from background blur, not directly visible.
outside_clip_unknowns: The propeller's actual operating state and speed before and after this cropped window, and any start/stop of rotation, are outside the segment and unknown.

do not invent a smooth transition or a causal mechanism to connect the two views.

and their relative positions before describing motion. Treat camera motion as uncertain when the
